summary: Missions and steps declare capacity: a mission's lane goes to each of its agents without one, and a step may only raise its seat's lane

replay.detail: No claim or projection changes. A run adds the mission's capacity to the agent declarations it materializes, so those seats are stored as if they had declared it.

schema.detail: MissionSpec and StepSpec gain an optional capacity field, omitted when absent, so an undeclared mission's revision and its steps' definition hashes are unchanged.

rules.detail: Publication refuses a step capacity below the lane of a seat the same publication declares (an undeclared seat counts at 1 core and 3G), an agentless step with a capacity, and a repeated or malformed capacity on a mission or step. A step's capacity is recorded but not yet applied: its seat keeps its own lane until admission lands. Publication refuses a mission revision that declares capacity until every current fleet member advertises mission_capacity.

compatibility.detail: An undeclared mission serializes exactly as before, so its revision is unchanged and an older member accepts it. An older member would refuse a mission revision that declares capacity on the mission or any step: it re-hashes a replicated mission.published body after reading it into its own MissionSpec, which drops the field, finds the revision invalid and quarantines the claim. So each daemon now advertises features.mission_capacity=1 on daemon.started, and publication (apply, its dry-run plan, and a direct mission.published append) refuses a new revision that declares capacity with mission-capacity-unavailable while any current fleet member has not advertised it, naming the member, or while an unfenced writer outside the membership replicates here. A host with no other member publishes at once. An older CLI refuses such a file at apply (unknown child).

downtime.detail: Takes effect for runs materialized after the daemon runs this build; lanes still need lanes = "on" on the host.

recovery.detail: Once a capacity-declaring revision is published, a member rolled back below this build refuses that revision and keeps the earlier one, until it upgrades again. Reverting the change makes an older parser refuse files that declare capacity on a mission or step; remove those blocks first. Seats already materialized keep the lane they were stored with until their run's next generation.
